cells.tense: Right now, with the pen, a shared thing is being felt from inside the way it breathes.
cells.act: read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop
cells.ask: Read the hardest part of a shared thing you belong to twice, slowly, before you change a word — first for what it carried for the people who made it, then for what it carries in this room.
cells.core:
Here, a shared thing — the ritual your people keep, the words said the way they have been said — can be entered and left as it is. When something in it shifts, no announcement or defense is needed. What was carrying the weight and what was only habit around it become visible by themselves.

Read the hardest part twice, slowly, before you change a word — first for what it carried for the people who made it, then for what it carries in this room. Nothing has to be decided. This is what the quiet of this draw is for — letting a meaning finish before you touch it. The shared thing goes on being shared while you do it, and you come out knowing which threads still hold and which have gone slack.
cells.sheetLine: Let the tradition read you back before you change it.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart knows before it moves
cells.place: the shared thing a group keeps alive and hands on

cells.tense: You are bracing to redraw a shared thing before it has finished arriving.
cells.ask: Before any redrawing, harvest what the change has already grown — a phrase, a practice, a new way the group holds something — and take it in as the crop ripening in the field.
cells.core:
The old shape is thinning under your hands, and your grip has already moved to the next version — who says what, which part stays, how it should look once you're done. Nobody else has been asked to go there yet, and most of the pressure is in your own head. The bracing blocks your view of what is already yours.

Before any redrawing, harvest what the change has already grown — a phrase, a practice, a new way the group holds something — and take it in as the crop ripening in the field. The redraw can come after the gathering. Waiting here isn't idle; the crop is made of it, and the others in this shared thing are living through the same season you are.

cells.tense: You are still at the door of a shared thing that already closed behind you.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Put what a shared thing meant to you into a single sentence, the truest you can find, and set it down where you will come across it again.
cells.core:
A shared thing has ended or gone quiet, and you are still where it used to be — the words held in your mouth, the slot kept open, the chair reserved for people who moved on. The quiet here is not indifference; it is what a room feels like after company has gone, and you're in it.

Put what it meant to you into a single sentence, the truest you can find, and set it down where you will come across it again. Don't wait for the right words to be handed over; put your own down. The line is small and it belongs to you, and the waiting can end where the line begins. Something written down can be picked up later, and that is what is being offered here.
cells.sheetLine: The shared thing ended. You're still at the door.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart knows before it moves
cells.place: the shared thing a group keeps alive and hands on

cells.tense: You are carrying a shared thing forward through your own continuance, without signing for it.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: Follow what you actually believe the shared thing is for — past the respectable version and the polite one — until you land on the plain answer, flattering or not.
cells.core:
The shared thing continues because you continue it — the tone, the way the words get said, the small practices nobody has asked about in years. Ask what you think it's for and you'd give the respectable answer; the real one is doing the work underneath, and you have not put your name to it. This continuance has an author, and the author's story is that the thing simply happens.

Follow what you actually believe the shared thing is for — past the respectable version and the polite one — until you land on the plain answer, flattering or not. Nothing has to change yet. The one who kept it level can look at what was kept, and this becomes a decision instead of a habit.

attempts.check: The strongest unsupported claim in my draft is that a shared meaning or tradition has settled into the person's own feeling life and is being kept alive by their presence — the record gives resonance and stillness at the seed, but it cannot say the person is the keeper of any particular tradition, nor that others notice it. A reader could reasonably say the still thing is not a tradition at all but a relationship or a private calm, and the reading would land differently. My asks survive being wrong because each is the person's own medicine returned to themselves — counting what an ending grew, reading one hard page slowly, putting two thoughts into one line, sorting pieces into a shape — all useful whether or not a shared meaning is what the card is holding. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the one that claims others can feel the weight you keep steady; I kept it thin here, drawn from the card's own tradition transmissibility, and left it out of the asks, where another person would only adorn the act.

attempts.check: The strongest unsupported claim is still that a shared meaning or tradition is what carries the person's feeling life and that others can feel the weight of it — the record gives resonance and stillness at the seed, not the keeper of any named tradition, and not anyone else's notice. A reader could reasonably say the still thing is a relationship or a private calm rather than a group practice, and much of the reading would survive that shift because each ask is the person's own medicine turned on their own material. That said, the asks hold even if the seat is wrong: reading a hard page slowly, counting what a change already grew, sorting scattered pieces into one line, and following a thought past its comfortable stop are useful whatever the material actually is. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the one that claims the keeping is felt by others around the table; I have left it out and kept the noticing with the person themselves.
